newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF sees full year sales up three pct.
newsitem.headline: BASF sees full year sales up three pct.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group BASF AG said on Wednesday it expects full-year 1996 sales to show a three percent rise and pre-tax profits to be at least as high as year-ago levels.
The group also reported an 8.8 percent rise in group nine-month pre-tax profits to 3.37 billion marks, but said third-quarter pre-tax profits slipped 2.3 percent to 1.05 billion marks.
Looking ahead, BASF said it expected a slight pickup in business activity to continue in the first months of 1997.
BASF said business picked up after the summer months and that sales in Germany, particularly gas sales, contributed to a rise in third quarter sales.
Sales climbed 7.2 percent to 11.85 billion marks in the third quarter while they rose only 2.9 percent to 36.1 billion marks in the first nine months of the year.
Referring to the third quarter numbers, BASF said: "For the first time this year, business in Germany, boosted particularly through gas sales, contributed to the overall increase."
While volume sales climbed 3.7 percent during the first nine months of the year, they were offset by a three percent drop in prices, BASF said.
Even as sales picked up again after the summer holiday months, prices remained under pressure, the group added.
Additionally BASF benefitted from more favourable foreign exchange rates, only one year after suffering from the mark's persistent strength.
Acquisitions and disinvestments also contributed to results, the group said.
Among the group's businesses, health and nutrition, growing 18.4 percent, and oil and gas, rising 12.4 percent, contributed to nine-month growth.
